text:
alex.sre: Quick heads-up — we're publishing a change to the SLO fallback policy. Planned rollout window: tomorrow 2024-07-20 03:00-03:30 UTC. This enables automatic fallback to the `fallback-quantized-v1` model variant when p99 latency > 450ms for > 3 minutes on a route. Link: https://go/internal/slo-fallback (internal docs)
jess.prod: Is this going to affect customers on Dedicated or Private? Any data egress implications?
alex.sre: Good q. No customer-visible config changes. Dedicated/Private keep the same model bundles unless the tenant has explicitly disabled fallbacks; doc explains the opt-out. No egress changes.
dan.infra: Oncall checklist? Who's watching dashboards for the first canary?
alex.sre: Canaries run in us-west first at 02:45 UTC (15m), then global at 03:00 if green. @jess.prod and @dan.infra please watch token-latency/p99 and error-rate/5m. Runbook: see snippet below.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered by alex.sre — build #a12b3c -> canary-us-west
maya.mlops: Short rationale: last week's KV cache thrash caused p99 spikes. Fallback reduces avg exec path and KV pressure; quality regression measured ~0.8% on our eval set (acceptable for failsafe).
jess.prod: What's the rollback condition?
alex.sre: Auto rollback if client-error-rate rises > 1.0% above baseline for >5m OR user-facing token-delta regressions exceed threshold in QA metrics. Also manual abort via `#/deploy cancel a12b3c`.
dan.infra: Runbook excerpt (paste):
```
# Oncall runbook — SLO fallback
1) Check dashboards: token-latency/p99, error-rate/5m, model-variant-fallback-rate
2) If p99 >450ms and fallback-rate=0 -> escalate to runtime oncall and trigger rollout
3) If error-rate spike -> rollback: `deploy rollback a12b3c`
4) If regressions in QA metric -> engage MLops (maya.mlops)
```
infra-bot: Canary us-west started at 2024-07-20T02:45:12Z — canary-id=cny-20240720-02
slo-bot: SLO config updated: route-tag=prod, p99_threshold=450ms, sustained_window=180s, fallback_variant=fallback-quantized-v1
jess.prod: We'll also exclude scheduled loadtests right? Don't want false positives
alex.sre: Yes — `traffic-tag: loadtest` is excluded from auto-fallback. Reminder: if you're running an intentional loadtest, set `test-mode=true` in the header.
maya.mlops: Quick perf numbers from internal bench: fallback reduces avg GPU time by ~19% and p99 tail shifts left ~120ms under KV pressure.
jess.prod: Thanks — I'll coordinate comms to platform teams and update the runbook link in the oncall doc.
alex.sre: TL;DR: scheduled window tomorrow 03:00-03:30 UTC, staged canary 02:45, exclusion for loadtests, rollback conditions listed in runbook. Ping if you want to observe the canary live.
jess.prod: ack :thumbsup:
dan.infra: i'll be on watch for the 02:45 canary, posting alerts channel if anything odd.
alex.sre: Appreciate it. If anything unexpected, mention `@sre-oncall` and escalate.
